title: Positive Ext obstruction to the Brown compactness clause
statement: Let X be a scheme, Λ a commutative condensed coefficient ring, S its bounded constructible finite-Tor property, and L=Loc(S) [sk-def-localizing-closure]. Let K be an object of L whose underlying derived object lies in S. Let F be a module object over Λ_X whose degree-zero image lies in L. If for every natural n there is a nonzero map K→F[0][n+1] in the ambient derived category, then BrownHypothesesFor Λ X does not hold. This is conditional on the nonzero maps, and asserts no field-cohomology computation.

source.place: finite-support compactness obstruction in not_preservesColimitsOfShape_of_forall_hom_ne_zero; applied to the Brown compactness clause

proof.text: Apply the varying-heart eventual-vanishing theorem to the constant sequence F_n=F. It supplies N such that every map K→F[0][n] is zero for n≥N. The supplied nonzero map in degree N+1 contradicts this bound. The varying-heart theorem constructs and restricts the required product-coproduct, using exact countable products.

theorem not_brownHypothesesFor_of_positive_ext
    {Λ : Sheaf (coherentTopology Profinite.{u}) Ab.{u + 1}}
    [MonObj Λ] [IsCommMonObj Λ] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (K : (localizingClosureProEtale Λ X).FullSubcategory)
    (hK : constantModelBoundedConstructible Λ X K.obj ∧
      DerivedCategory.finiteTorAmplitude _ K.obj)
    (F : Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1}) (condensedRingObj Λ X))
    (hF : localizingClosureProEtale Λ X ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj F))
    (hExt : ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ f : K.obj ⟶
      ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj F)⟦((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ)⟧, f ≠ 0) :
    ¬ BrownHypothesesFor Λ X
